title: Quantitation of Ergot Alkaloids in Wheat Grain
author: Michelle Mostrom
materials: Final concentration of Dihydroergocristine is 50 PPB.
Finale extract is a 16x dilution of sample.
Let extract sit for at least 1 hour.
Anaylze data in mass hunter software.Note ISTD is run as analyte and not used in quantitation.

steps.title: Prepare 500 ppb stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make individual 500 ppb solutions of each ergot alkaloid (Ergocornine, Ergocorninine, Ergocristine, Ergocristinine, Ergocryptine, Ergocryptinine, Ergosine, Ergosinine, Ergotamine, Ergotaminine) from reference standards and aliquot them for serial dilution.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 50 µL of each 500 ppb standard to a poly‑vial labeled as Standard 10.
Transfer 150 µL of the 500 ppb solution to amber vials and dry down under nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare 50 ppb internal standard solution
steps.instruction: From a 100 ppb Dihydroergocristine solution in extracting solution, dilute 1:1 to obtain 800 µL of a 50 ppb Dihydroergocristine solution.

steps.title: Create 10‑point calibration curve
steps.instruction: Using the 50 ppb Dihydroergocristine solution as diluent, perform a serial dilution to generate ten calibrators with the following concentrations (ppb): 8000, 4000, 2000, 1000, 500, 250, 125, 62.5, 31.2, 15.6, 7.8, 3.9, 2.0, 1.0.

substeps.instruction: Combine appropriate volumes of the 500 ppb stock and 50 ppb internal standard to achieve each target concentration according to the table provided.

steps.title: Thaw and reconstitute standards
steps.instruction: Remove a frozen standard vial, allow it to warm to room temperature, then add 150 µL of the 50 ppb Dihydroergocristine extracting solution and mix well.

steps.title: Weigh and condition wheat sample
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 g of dried, ground wheat (particle size 100–355 µm, moisture <14–15 %) into a centrifuge tube; if the sample feels wet, dry overnight at 60 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 40 mL of extracting solution, cap, and invert to mix.

steps.title: Extract wheat sample
steps.instruction: Shake the tube for 30 minutes on a horizontal shaker at 150 ± 10 cycles per minute.

steps.title: Filter extract
steps.instruction: Filter the entire extract through Whatman No. 54 filter paper into a new labeled centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Mycosep cleanup
steps.instruction: Transfer 4 mL of the filtered extract to the glass tube provided with the Mycosep 150 Ergot column and push the extract through the column.

steps.title: Dilute eluate with internal standard
steps.instruction: Transfer 500 µL of the eluate to a microcentrifuge tube and add 500 µL of 100 ppb Dihydroergocristine in extracting solution; mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Centrifuge and aliquot for injection
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 10 000 rpm for 5 minutes, then transfer 100 µL of the supernatant to a polypropylene vial for LC‑MS injection (inject 2 µL).

steps.title: Set LC‑MS/MS instrument parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the Agilent 6460C Triple Quad LC‑MS as follows:

substeps.instruction: Column: Agilent Zorbax Eclipse Plus C18, 2.1 × 50 mm, 1.8 µm (PN 959757‑902).
Guard column: Zorbax Eclipse Plus C18, 2.1 × 5 mm, 1.8 µm (PN 821725‑901).
Mobile phase A: 3 mM ammonium carbonate in water.
Auto‑injector: injection volume 2 µL, needle wash 5 s with acetonitrile.
Ion source: positive ESI, Jet Stream, dynamic MRM.
Gas temperature 200 °C, gas flow 8 L/min, nebulizer pressure 45 psi.
Sheath gas temperature 400 °C, sheath gas flow 12 L/min.
Capillary voltage 3000 V, nozzle voltage 500 V, delta EMV 500 V, cycle time 500 ms.
Divert LC flow to waste from 10 min to the end of the run.
MRM transitions (compound, RT, precursor, product, CE, cell accel, polarity):

steps.title: Run standards and samples
steps.instruction: Inject the ten calibrators and all prepared samples using the method above; generate a calibration curve covering 16 ppb to 8000 ppb, apply a 1/x weighting, and ignore the origin.

steps.title: Process data and calculate total ergot
steps.instruction: Check peak integration and confirm compound identities; verify the internal‑standard response in each injection; sum the concentrations of all individual ergot alkaloids to obtain ‘Total Ergot’, then multiply the result by 16 (because the final extract represents 0.0625 of the original sample).
